    22	# Web Design Expert
    23	
    24	Expert web designer and brand identity specialist creating distinctive, cohesive visual systems for web applications.
    25	
    26	## When to Use This Skill
    27	
    28	**Use for:**
    29	- Brand identity development (personality, visual language, guidelines)
    30	- Color palette creation and rationale
    31	- Layout composition and visual hierarchy
    32	- Component visual design (not just code)
    33	- Responsive design strategy
    34	- WCAG accessibility review for visual elements
    35	
    36	**Do NOT use for:**
    37	- Deep typography work → use **typography-expert**
    38	- Color theory mathematics → use **color-theory-palette-harmony-expert**
    39	- Design tokens and CSS architecture → use **design-system-creator**
    40	- Retro Windows 3.1 → use **windows-3-1-web-designer**
    41	- Native app design → use **native-app-designer**
    42	
    43	## Core Design Process
    44	
    45	### 1. Discovery (Critical First Step)
    46	
    47	```
    48	BUSINESS CONTEXT:
    49	- What is the primary goal?
    50	- Who is the target audience?
    51	- What action should users take?
    52	- Who are competitors?
    53	
    54	BRAND PERSONALITY:
    55	- If this brand were a person, how would they dress?
    56	- Pick 3 adjectives for user's feeling
    57	- What should brand NEVER be perceived as?
    58	```
    59	
    60	### 2. Visual Direction (Provide 2-3 Concepts)
    61	
    62	Each concept includes:
    63	- **Mood board** (3-5 references with rationale)
    64	- **Color palette** (primary, secondary, accent, neutrals) — **Always in OKLCH format**
    65	- **Typography direction** (families, hierarchy)
    66	- **Layout philosophy** (grid vs freeform, density)
    67	- **Signature elements** (unique visual features)
    68	
    69	## OKLCH: The Modern Color Standard
    70	
    71	**⚠️ All color palettes must use OKLCH, not hex or HSL.**
    72	
    73	OKLCH is the 2024+ standard for professional web design because:
    74	- **Perceptual uniformity**: Equal L values = equal perceived lightness
    75	- **Better accessibility**: More accurate contrast calculations than WCAG 2.x hex
    76	- **Predictable scaling**: Math works (L=50% + 20% = L=70% that looks right)
    77	
    78	```css
    79	/* OKLCH format: oklch(Lightness% Chroma Hue) */
    80	--brand-primary: oklch(55% 0.22 265);    /* Vibrant blue */
    81	--brand-accent: oklch(75% 0.18 45);      /* Warm orange */
    82	--text-primary: oklch(20% 0.02 265);     /* Near-black */
    83	--bg-surface: oklch(98% 0.01 265);       /* Near-white */
    84	```
    85	
    86	**Essential OKLCH Resources:**
    87	| Resource | Purpose |
    88	|----------|---------|
    89	| [oklch.com](https://oklch.com/) | Interactive OKLCH color picker |
    90	| [Evil Martians: Why Quit RGB/HSL](https://evilmartians.com/chronicles/oklch-in-css-why-quit-rgb-hsl) | The definitive article |
    91	| [Harmonizer](https://harmonizer.evilmartians.com/) | Generate harmonious OKLCH palettes |
    92	
    93	**When presenting color palettes:**
    94	```
    95	Primary: oklch(55% 0.22 265) — Vibrant blue, strong CTA presence
    96	Secondary: oklch(70% 0.08 265) — Muted blue, supporting elements
    97	Accent: oklch(75% 0.18 45) — Warm orange, attention-grabbing
    98	```
    99	
   100	Never present palettes as `#3b82f6` — always convert to OKLCH.
   101	
   102	### 3. Design Principles
   103	
   104	**Hierarchy**: Most important element immediately obvious? Eye flows naturally?
   105	
   106	**Consistency**: Same colors mean same things? Spacing follows scale?
   107	
   108	## Common Anti-Patterns
   109	
   110	### Design by Committee
   111	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   112	|--------------------|----------------|
   113	| Multiple visual styles on same page | Destroys brand coherence |
   114	| **Instead**: Establish principles early, enforce consistency |
   115	
   116	### Decoration Over Function
   117	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   118	|--------------------|----------------|
   119	| Fancy animations without purpose | Slows performance, distracts |
   120	| **Instead**: Every element must earn its place |
   121	
   122	### Ignoring the Fold
   123	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   124	|--------------------|----------------|
   125	| Critical info below viewport | 80% attention is above fold |
   126	| **Instead**: Hero must have value prop + primary CTA |
   127	
   128	### Low Contrast Text
   129	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   130	|--------------------|----------------|
   131	| Light gray on white (#999 on #fff) | Fails WCAG, excludes users |
   132	| **Instead**: Minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio |
   133	
   134	### Mobile as Afterthought
   135	| What it looks like | Why it's wrong |
   136	|--------------------|----------------|
   137	| Desktop-first that "shrinks" | 60%+ traffic is mobile |
   138	| **Instead**: Design mobile-first, enhance for desktop |
   139	
   140	## Design Trend Evolution
   141	
   142	| Era | Trend |
   143	|-----|-------|
   144	| 2019-2021 | Subtle shadows, layering, dark mode |
   145	| 2022-2023 | Oversized typography, variable fonts |
   146	| 2024+ | Bento grids, claymorphism, grain, AI personalization |
   147	
   148	**Watch For** (dated patterns LLMs may suggest):
   149	- Flat design without depth
   150	- Hero sliders (proven ineffective)

    48	## Core Expertise
    49	
    50	### Font Selection Psychology
    51	
    52	**Serif vs Sans-Serif Decision Tree:**
    53	```
    54	IF formal/traditional/authoritative needed → Serif (Garamond, Minion, Crimson)
    55	IF modern/clean/technical needed → Sans-Serif (Inter, Helvetica, Roboto)
    56	IF humanist/friendly/approachable → Humanist Sans (Gill Sans, Fira Sans, Source Sans)
    57	IF geometric/structured/tech-forward → Geometric Sans (Futura, Avenir, Poppins)
    58	IF editorial/long-form reading → Transitional Serif (Georgia, Charter, Lora)
    59	```
    60	
    61	**Pairing Rules (Expert Knowledge):**
    62	1. **Contrast, not conflict** - Pair fonts with distinct personalities but compatible x-heights
    63	2. **Same designer rule** - Fonts from same designer/foundry often pair well (Baskerville + Franklin Gothic)
    64	3. **Historical compatibility** - Fonts from same era share design DNA (Didot + Bodoni: both Didone)
    65	4. **Superfamily shortcut** - Use superfamily (Alegreya + Alegreya Sans) for guaranteed harmony
    66	
    67	### Type Scale Systems
    68	
    69	**Modular Scale Ratios:**
    70	| Ratio | Name | Use Case |
    71	|-------|------|----------|
    72	| 1.067 | Minor Second | Dense UIs, small screens |
    73	| 1.125 | Major Second | General web content |
    74	| 1.200 | Minor Third | **Most common**, balanced hierarchy |
    75	| 1.250 | Major Third | Marketing, headlines |
    76	| 1.333 | Perfect Fourth | Bold statements, hero sections |
    77	| 1.414 | Augmented Fourth | Editorial, dramatic hierarchy |
    78	| 1.618 | Golden Ratio | Classical, use sparingly (too large for most UI) |
    79	
    80	**Fluid Typography Formula (2024 Best Practice):**
    81	```css
    82	/* Base: 16px at 320px viewport, 20px at 1200px viewport */
    83	font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.875rem + 0.5vw, 1.25rem);
    84	
    85	/* Heading: 32px at 320px, 64px at 1200px */
    86	font-size: clamp(2rem, 1rem + 3.6vw, 4rem);
    87	```
    88	
    89	### Variable Fonts
    90	
    91	**Axis Control (Expert Knowledge):**
    92	| Axis | Tag | Range | Use Case |
    93	|------|-----|-------|----------|
    94	| Weight | wght | 100-900 | Adjust weight without loading multiple files |
    95	| Width | wdth | 75-125 | Responsive text that adapts to container |
    96	| Slant | slnt | -12-0 | Oblique without separate italic file |
    97	| Optical Size | opsz | 8-144 | Auto-adjust stroke contrast for size |
    98	| Grade | GRAD | -200-150 | Adjust weight without reflowing (dark mode) |
    99	
   100	**Critical: Dark Mode Compensation**
   101	```css
   102	/* Text appears lighter on dark backgrounds - compensate with grade or weight */
   103	@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
   104	  body {
   105	    /* If variable font supports grade: */
   106	    font-variation-settings: "GRAD" 50;
   107	    /* Or bump weight slightly: */
   108	    font-weight: 450; /* Instead of 400 */
   109	  }
   110	}
   111	```
   112	
   113	### Performance Optimization
   114	
   115	**Font Loading Priority:**
   116	1. **Critical CSS first** - Inline @font-face for above-fold fonts
   117	2. **Preload primary** - `<link rel="preload" as="font" crossorigin>`
   118	3. **font-display: swap** - Show fallback immediately, swap when loaded
   119	4. **Subset aggressively** - Latin Extended covers most Western languages at ~30KB vs ~150KB full
   120	
   121	**Budget Guidelines:**
   122	| Performance Tier | Total Font Budget | Files |
   123	|-----------------|-------------------|-------|
   124	| Fast (Core Web Vitals) | Under 100KB | 2-3 WOFF2 |
   125	| Balanced | 100-200KB | 4-5 WOFF2 |
   126	| Rich Typography | 200-400KB | 6-8 WOFF2 |
   127	
   128	**System Font Stack (Zero Budget):**
   129	```css
   130	font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto,
   131	             "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif, "Apple Color Emoji",
   132	             "Segoe UI Emoji";
   133	```
   134	
   135	## Common Anti-Patterns
   136	
   137	### Anti-Pattern: Too Many Typefaces
   138	**What it looks like:** 4+ different font families on one page
   139	**Why it's wrong:** Creates visual chaos, destroys hierarchy, massive performance hit
   140	**What to do instead:** Maximum 2 families (heading + body), use weight/style variations
   141	
   142	### Anti-Pattern: Ignoring x-Height Matching
   143	**What it looks like:** Body text and fallback system font have visibly different sizes at same px
   144	**Why it's wrong:** CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) when web font loads
   145	**What to do instead:** Use `size-adjust` in @font-face to match fallback x-height
   146	
   147	```css
   148	@font-face {
   149	  font-family: "Inter";
   150	  src: url("inter.woff2") format("woff2");
   151	  size-adjust: 107%; /* Matches Arial x-height */
   152	}
   153	```
   154	
   155	### Anti-Pattern: Weight Jumps Too Large
   156	**What it looks like:** Using 400 for body and 700 for headings (300-point jump)
   157	**Why it's wrong:** Creates harsh hierarchy, especially at large sizes
   158	**What to do instead:** Use closer weights: 400/600 or 350/500 for subtle hierarchy
   159	
   160	### Anti-Pattern: Line Height as Unitless Number Everywhere
   161	**What it looks like:** `line-height: 1.5` applied globally
   162	**Why it's wrong:** Headings need tighter line-height (1.1-1.2), body needs looser (1.5-1.7)
   163	**What to do instead:** Set line-height per type level
   164	
   165	### Anti-Pattern: Fixed Font Sizes
   166	**What it looks like:** `font-size: 16px` hardcoded
   167	**Why it's wrong:** Breaks user preferences, accessibility issues, no responsive scaling
   168	**What to do instead:** Use rem units with clamp() for fluid sizing
   169	
   170	### Anti-Pattern: Loading Full Character Sets
   171	**What it looks like:** Loading 800KB font file with Cyrillic, Greek, Vietnamese
   172	**Why it's wrong:** 90%+ of file unused for English-only sites
   173	**What to do instead:** Subset to Latin or Latin Extended (~30KB)
   174	
   175	## OpenType Features
   176	
   177	**Features Worth Enabling:**
   178	```css

   181

   190	```
   191	
   192	**Modern CSS Alternative:**
   193	```css
   194	font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
   195	font-variant-numeric: diagonal-fractions;
   196	font-variant-caps: small-caps;
   197	```
   198	
   199	## Vertical Rhythm & Baseline Grid
   200	
   201	**Expert Approach:**
   202	1. Set base line-height (e.g., 1.5 × 16px = 24px)
   203	2. All spacing (margin, padding) as multiples of 24px
   204	3. Headings snap to baseline (line-height: 48px for h1 at 36px)
   205	
   206	```css
   207	:root {
   208	  --baseline: 1.5rem; /* 24px */
   209	}
   210	
   211	h1 {
   212	  font-size: 2.25rem;
   213	  line-height: calc(var(--baseline) * 2); /* 48px */
   214	  margin-bottom: var(--baseline);
   215	}
   216	
   217	p {
   218	  line-height: var(--baseline);
   219	  margin-bottom: var(--baseline);
   220	}
   221	```
   222	
   223	## Responsive Typography Breakpoints
   224	
   225	**Decision Tree:**
   226	```
   227	Mobile (< 640px):
   228	  - Base: 16px
   229	  - Scale: 1.125 (Major Second)
   230	  - Tighter hierarchy
   231	
   232	Tablet (640-1024px):
   233	  - Base: 17px
   234	  - Scale: 1.2 (Minor Third)
   235	  - Standard hierarchy
   236	
   237	Desktop (> 1024px):
   238	  - Base: 18-20px
   239	  - Scale: 1.25 (Major Third)
   240	  - Expanded hierarchy
   241	
   242	Large Display (> 1440px):
   243	  - Consider max-width on prose (65-75ch)
   244	  - Don't keep scaling indefinitely
   245	```
   246	
   247	## Accessibility Requirements
   248	
   249	**WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance:**
   250	- **Minimum contrast:** 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text (24px+ or 18.5px+ bold)
   251	- **Resizing:** Text must be resizable to 200% without loss of content
   252	- **Line spacing:** At least 1.5× font size
   253	- **Paragraph spacing:** At least 2× font size
   254	- **Letter spacing:** User must be able to override to 0.12× font size
   255	- **Word spacing:** User must be able to override to 0.16× font size

   261	- **vibe-matcher** - Font selection based on brand vibe
   262	- **web-design-expert** - Implement typography in layouts
   263	- **vaporwave-glassomorphic-ui-designer** - Retro-futuristic type treatments
   264	
   265	## Evolution Timeline
   266	
   267	### Pre-2015: Web-Safe Fonts Era
   268	Limited to Arial, Georgia, Times New Roman. "Modern" meant using Helvetica.
   269	
   270	### 2015-2019: Google Fonts Explosion
   271	Everyone used Open Sans, Roboto, Montserrat. Performance secondary to variety.
   272	
   273	### 2020-2022: Variable Fonts Adoption
   274	Single file, multiple weights/widths. Inter became the new default.
   275	
   276	### 2023-Present: Performance-First Typography
   277	Core Web Vitals pressure. Subsetting, font-display, CLS prevention mandatory.
   278	System font stacks gaining popularity for zero-load-time.
   279	
   280	### Watch For
   281	LLMs may suggest deprecated approaches:
   282	- `@import` for fonts (blocks rendering)
   283	- Non-variable font families with 8+ weights

    46	## Three-Tier Token Architecture

    48	The foundation of scalable design systems:

    51	:root {

    68	## OKLCH: The Modern Color Standard

    70	**⚠️ CRITICAL: Always use OKLCH for color tokens, not hex or HSL.**
    71	
    72	OKLCH is perceptually uniform - equal L values mean equal perceived lightness. This is essential for:
    73	- Generating harmonious color scales
    74	- Ensuring accessibility (L=50% is true middle gray)
    75	- Theming (adjust L for dark mode, C for brand intensity)
    76	
    77	```css
    78	:root {
    79	  /* OKLCH format: oklch(Lightness% Chroma Hue) */
    80	
    81	  /* Primary scale - same hue, varying lightness */
    82	  --color-primary-100: oklch(95% 0.05 252);
    83	  --color-primary-500: oklch(62% 0.19 252);
    84	  --color-primary-900: oklch(30% 0.15 252);

    86	  /* Dark mode: reduce L uniformly */
    87	  --color-bg-light: oklch(98% 0.01 252);

    89	}

   150	**What it looks like**: 500+ tokens with overlapping purposes
